title: A Trump-backed crypto firm is helping sell the very Chinese AI his government is trying to block
excerpt: World Liberty Financial, the Trump family crypto venture, is behind WorldClaw, a Hong Kong platform reselling AI models from US-restricted Chinese firms, payable in its USD1 stablecoin.
content_html:
A crypto venture backed by Donald Trump and his family is helping to bankroll a platform that resells artificial intelligence from Chinese companies the US government has blacklisted, an arrangement that sits awkwardly beside the administration’s own campaign to choke off China’s AI industry.

Reuters reported on Monday that World Liberty Financial, the Trump-linked crypto firm, is behind WorldClaw, a Hong Kong-based service offering access to models from developers Washington has flagged as security risks.

WorldClaw’s pitch is a menu of roughly 90 AI models, of which about 43 come from Chinese companies.

They reportedly include Alibaba and Baidu, both designated by the Pentagon as aligned with China’s military, and Z.ai, which is subject to US Commerce Department export restrictions.

The line-up is also said to feature DeepSeek and Moonshot, two labs that American officials have accused of building their systems on stolen US technology. Models from OpenAI and Anthropic sit on the very same shelf.

The financial plumbing is what turns an unremarkable AI reseller into a political problem.

Customers can pay for WorldClaw using USD1, World Liberty Financial’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, and each such transaction stands to benefit the venture, in which the Trump family is reported to hold a stake of around 38%.

Put plainly, the president’s family could earn from Americans buying access to the Chinese AI that the president’s own government is straining to keep out.

That is the crux of the discomfort. The administration has made countering Chinese AI a centrepiece of policy, from export controls on advanced chips to public accusations that Chinese labs are copying American models at industrial scale.

A Trump-branded venture positioned to profit from selling those same models is, at the very least, an unusually literal collision between public policy and private interest.

The tension is not abstract: the harder the administration pushes to restrict a given Chinese lab, the more valuable a frictionless way to buy its models quietly becomes.

World Liberty and WorldClaw reject that framing. The two say they operate independently of one another, and that listing an AI model does not amount to endorsing its developer, no more than an app store vouches for every app it carries.

The White House, for its part, has repeatedly maintained that Trump acts only in the public interest and holds no conflicts of interest, a position it restated in response to the reporting.

World Liberty Financial has become the most lucrative and most scrutinised of the family’s crypto ventures.

It has drawn attention both for the scale of money involved and for the unusual company it has sometimes kept, and the president’s crypto holdings have swelled into the billions on paper even as ethics lawyers warn about the fading line between the family business and the office he holds.

The firm has lately pushed deeper into the mainstream too, winning preliminary US approval for a national bank charter tied to the same USD1 stablecoin that now doubles as a payment rail for WorldClaw.

The WorldClaw arrangement crystallises a tension the crypto and AI booms keep throwing up: rules written in Washington, money made everywhere else.

Stablecoins move value across borders with almost no friction, and a reseller in Hong Kong can offer a restricted Chinese model to a buyer in Ohio in a few clicks.

Export controls were built for shipping containers and data centres, not for a checkout page settled in a president-linked token.

None of this is unlawful on its face, and WorldClaw is far from the only route to a Chinese model. But the optics are striking, and the episode will sharpen an already loud argument about whether the Trump family’s crypto empire can sit comfortably alongside the powers of the presidency.

For now, the same government trying to wall off Chinese AI has a first family placed, however indirectly, to take a cut when Americans buy it regardless.

content_html_zh:
由唐纳德·特朗普及其家族支持的一家加密货币企业正在帮助资助一个平台，该平台转售来自美国政府列入黑名单的中国公司的人工智能，这一安排与政府自己遏制中国人工智能行业的行动显得尴尬。

路透社周一报道称，与特朗普有联系的加密货币公司 World Liberty Financial 是 WorldClaw 的幕后黑手，WorldClaw 是一项总部位于香港的服务，可访问华盛顿已标记为安全风险的开发商的模型。

WorldClaw 的宣传菜单包含大约 90 个人工智能模型，其中约 43 个来自中国公司。

据报道，其中包括被五角大楼指定为与中国军方结盟的阿里巴巴和百度，以及受到美国商务部出口限制的再爱科技。

据说该阵容还包括 DeepSeek 和 Moonshot，美国官员指责这两个实验室利用窃取的美国技术构建系统。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的模型位于同一个架子上。

正是财务管道将一个不起眼的人工智能经销商变成了一个政治问题。

客户可以使用 World Liberty Financial 与美元挂钩的稳定币 USD1 来支付 WorldClaw，每笔此类交易都将使该企业受益，据报道，特朗普家族持有该企业约 38% 的股份。

简单地说，总统的家人可以通过美国人购买中国人工智能来赚钱，而总统自己的政府正竭尽全力阻止其进入。

这就是不舒服的症结所在。 政府已将打击中国人工智能作为政策的核心，从先进芯片的出口管制到公开指责中国实验室在工业规模上复制美国模式。

一家特朗普品牌的企业定位于通过销售这些相同型号来获利，这至少是公共政策与私人利益之间不同寻常的字面冲突。

这种紧张关系并不是抽象的：政府越严厉地限制某个中国实验室，悄悄地购买其模型的无摩擦方式就变得越有价值。

World Liberty 和 WorldClaw 拒绝接受这种框架。 两人表示，他们彼此独立运营，列出人工智能模型并不等于认可其开发者，就像应用程序商店为其提供的每个应用程序提供担保一样。

白宫方面一再坚称特朗普的行为只符合公共利益，不存在利益冲突，并在回应报道时重申了这一立场。

World Liberty Financial 已成为该家族加密货币企业中最赚钱、最受审查的企业。

它因其涉及的资金规模和它有时保留的不寻常的公司而引起了人们的关注，尽管道德律师警告称，总统的加密资产持有量已经激增至纸面上的数十亿美元，尽管道德律师警告称，家族企业与他所担任的办公室之间的界限正在逐渐消失。

该公司最近也更深入地融入主流，赢得了美国对与同一个 1 美元稳定币挂钩的国家银行执照的初步批准，该稳定币现在兼作 WorldClaw 的支付渠道。

WorldClaw 的安排体现了加密货币和人工智能繁荣不断引发的紧张局势：规则在华盛顿制定，金钱在其他地方赚钱。

稳定币几乎可以毫无摩擦地跨境转移价值，香港的经销商只需点击几下鼠标就可以向俄亥俄州的买家提供受限制的中国模式。

出口管制是针对集装箱和数据中心建立的，而不是针对与总统相关的代币结算的结账页面。

从表面上看，这一切都不违法，而 WorldClaw 远非通向中国模式的唯一途径。 但这一事件令人震惊，这一事件将加剧关于特朗普家族的加密货币帝国能否与总统权力并驾齐驱的激烈争论。

目前，试图阻止中国人工智能发展的政府却让第一家庭在美国人购买人工智能产品时（不管是间接的）分得一杯羹。
